note: The British Indian Ocean Territory's Road Traffic Ordinance 1998 (the revised edition the Administration publishes on biot.gov.io, read 2026-10-30), s 4: a driver must hold a current licence issued by a competent authority in the United Kingdom, the United States, a Commonwealth country, a member of the European Union or the European Economic Area, Switzerland or a country the Commissioner names by notice, or under an international convention the United Kingdom or the United States is party to, or, for the United States Government's vehicles only, by its forces in the Territory. The Ordinance gives no licence of the Territory's own: it is held as issuing none, drivers there holding one from elsewhere (the lead, 2026-10-30, when the form took a place issuing no licence). Which foreign licences it accepts isn't held.

sources.title: British Indian Ocean Territory, The Road Traffic Ordinance 1998 (Revised Ordinances of the British Indian Ocean Territory)
sources.said: THE ROAD TRAFFIC ORDINANCE 1998 ... To comply with this subsection, a driving licence must be current and must have been issued ... by a competent authority in ... the United Kingdom ... the United States of America ... any country that is a member of the Commonwealth

sources.title: British Indian Ocean Territory Administration, Revised Ordinances
